publications.assertionSummary: Occupation: 'Tailor … the 1661 Braintree deed in which he is styled "John Gurney, tailor."'

incoming.explanation: Weighs the Monatiquot freehold as the second distinct parcel.
The estate's silence on tailoring equipment qualifies how central the 'tailor' occupation of the 1661/2 Thayer deed was to John's economy at death (cross-topic to braintree-community).
The 12 February 1661/2 deed styling 'John Gurney, tailor' is the direct documentary evidence of the trade.

outgoing.explanation: Deed associates (Brackett, Rockwell) show community ties.
Owned and sold a Braintree freehold, 1661/2.

sources.excerpt: John Gurney, tailor … unto Richard Thayer … house and orchard … on the Monatiquot

sources.alignmentNote: Suffolk Deeds registry copy of the 1661/2 Gurney-Thayer conveyance read via FamilySearch full-text search ('John Gurney of Braintry Taylor'); second manuscript-registry representation of the deed printed by Bates and in Suffolk Deeds Liber IV.
sources.locator: Suffolk Deeds registry copy (FamilySearch full-text; AI-transcribed image)

statement: On 12 February 1661/2 "John Gurney, tailor" conveyed to Richard Thayer, for £14, a Braintree house and orchard, a five-acre Monatiquot-River parcel, and an adjoining half-acre; possession given 16 April 1662, signed by mark, witnessed by Peter Brackett and John Rockwell.
